approach: Write docs/spec.toml as an array of [[requirement]] tables (id, statement, kind, status, optional supersedes, [[requirement.source]] with quote + heading) plus an [[open_question]] array, covering only Olympus sections 1-6 (~35 compact requirements, short quotes, merged duplicates). Add xtask/tests/spec.rs: a pure `check(spec_text, brief_text) -> Vec<String>` over serde structs (toml already a dev-dependency), whitespace-collapsed substring matching, id uniqueness, supersedes targets, at-least-one-source, kind/status enums, open-question quotes. Tests: the real spec passes; four in-memory negative cases; heading coverage for R1-R8 and Olympus sections 1-5; open-question presence. Record D111, CHANGELOG, an enforcement row (M33) and an ontology term. Keep all text free of the policy scanner's banned words.

decisions.choice: TOML parsed by the existing toml + serde dev-dependencies; checker lives in xtask/tests/spec.rs as a pure function over strings, so negative cases are in-memory.
decisions.reason: Buy-first: toml and serde are already workspace dev-dependencies of xtask. A pure function lets the negative cases mutate the real spec text without touching files.

rejected.why: Quotes and fields would need a hand-written parser; structure is unenforced.
No comments, awkward multi-line quotes, noisy for Sri to approve.
Implicit typing pitfalls, and a new dependency; the repo already uses TOML for data.

decisions.choice: Quote matching collapses all whitespace runs to single spaces on both sides, then uses a plain substring test. Quotes avoid table pipes and bullet markers by quoting within one line or sentence.
decisions.reason: Matches the acceptance wording and tolerates line wraps; keeps quotes short and cheap to verify.

rejected.why: Would let paraphrases pass; 'verbatim' must be exact.

decisions.choice: Coverage test counts requirements by the `heading` field of their sources (headings like '6. Requirements for systemic learning / R1 — Causal investigation', '1. Vision'). Heading strings must themselves appear in BRIEF.md as heading lines (checked by matching the last path component against a '#'-prefixed line).
decisions.reason: Makes criterion 3 about sources' headings, and stops invented headings.

decisions.choice: Open questions as [[open_question]] with id, question, and two or more [[open_question.source]] quotes; checker verifies each quote. Writer includes one only if sections 1-6 truly conflict or leave a choice open (candidate: Section 5 'Neither loop owns the other' beside Section 2 Athena owning 'improves plans and engineering methods'? only if the producer judges it a real conflict); otherwise a top-level `no_open_questions_reason` string says none exist, and a unit test with an in-memory open question proves the field is checked.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 allows either; avoids inventing conflicts.

rejected.option: Invent a conflict to fill the field

decisions.choice: Enforcement row M33 and one ontology term 'spec' (sources: docs/spec.toml, the new decision id, relation to 'Sri'), each citing real test names.
decisions.reason: Both files are listed deliverables; M24 requires named tests exist, so names must match spec.rs exactly.

files.purpose: The spec: requirements and open questions from Olympus sections 1-6, each with verbatim quotes and headings.
Checker `check(spec, brief)` and tests: real spec passes, four negative cases, heading coverage, open-question handling.
Nothing to add if toml and serde already resolve (they are already dev-dependencies); touch only if the producer finds a missing feature. Cargo.lock stays unchanged then.
Only if a dependency changes; expected unchanged.
Add an Added entry under [Unreleased] for the spec and its checking test.
Append D111: spec format, TOML versus Markdown with ids, JSON, YAML, and the second-job note for sections 7-10, governing philosophy and 2026-10-17 addenda.
Add row M33: the spec's quotes are verbatim, ids unique, targets exist; blocks and allows list the real test names in spec.rs.
Add a `spec` term with its misread, sources docs/spec.toml and D111, and a relation to an existing term.

steps: Re-read BRIEF.md lines 550-862 and policy.rs boundary_words/boundary_fragments (lines 88-135) to avoid banned words in statements and quotes.

Draft docs/spec.toml: header comment on format; [[requirement]] with id (e.g. V-01, P-01, F-01, E-01, L-01, R1-01), statement, kind, status = "active", optional supersedes, and [[requirement.source]] quote + heading; merge duplicates (e.g. 'independent evaluation' in R4 and Section 5 stage E) into one requirement with several sources; add [[open_question]] entries or the none-found reason.

Write xtask/tests/spec.rs: serde structs with deny_unknown_fields; whitespace normalizer; `check(spec_text, brief_text) -> Vec<String>` covering quote, unique id, supersedes, nonempty sources, enums, heading present in BRIEF.md, open-question quotes.
Add tests: the_spec_matches_the_brief, four negative tests, every_requirement_area_has_a_requirement, open-question tests (real or in-memory).
Confirm xtask/Cargo.toml already supplies toml and serde; change it only if needed.
Add CHANGELOG entry, D111 in docs/decisions.md, M33 row in docs/enforcement.md and the `spec` term in docs/ontology.toml.
Run cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked; fix findings.

risks.risk: A quote copied with markdown markers, curly quotes or a line wrap differs from BRIEF.md and fails.
risks.mitigation: Keep quotes short, one line each, copy from BRIEF.md lines 560-862, avoid table rows and pipes; the test reports the exact failing quote.

risks.risk: Quoted BRIEF text or spec statements contain a word the boundary scan bans (e.g. 'handoffs' in the Hermes row, 'lease', 'sandbox'), failing policy.rs.
risks.mitigation: Do not mention operators, hand-offs or places Athena runs; avoid the banned words even in quotes (Section 2's 'handoffs' in Hermes's row is a banned-word form, so do not quote that row's tail; check policy words in policy.rs lines 88-130 first). Run the policy test.

risks.risk: A long spec makes verification slow, the cause of the previous failure.
risks.mitigation: Cap at about 35 requirements, one per idea, one or two short sources each.

risks.risk: M24 fails if the enforcement row names a test that does not exist.
risks.mitigation: Put test names in enforcement.md exactly as defined in spec.rs; run policy tests.

risks.risk: The ontology check rejects the new term (missing field, unknown source or relation target).
risks.mitigation: Fill every required field with a concrete misread and valid sources; use existing term names for relations.

demonstrations.method: Run the xtask spec test against the real docs/spec.toml and BRIEF.md.
demonstrations.observes: `the_spec_matches_the_brief` passes with an empty list of problems.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the checker did not verify quotes, ids, supersedes and sources, or the spec had a misquoted or sourceless requirement, the test `the_spec_matches_the_brief` fails.

demonstrations.method: Four in-memory tests mutate the real spec text: altered quote, duplicated id, bad supersedes, removed sources; each asserts the checker reports that specific problem. One further asserts the unmodified text yields none.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without each check, the matching negative test would find no problem and its assertion that the problem list names the fault would fail.

demonstrations.method: Group requirements by their sources' headings and assert at least one each for R1..R8 and sections 1-5 (Vision, Pantheon, Feedback, Example, lifecycle).
demonstrations.observes: `every_requirement_area_has_a_requirement` passes; the counts are asserted nonzero.
demonstrations.fails_without: If R1-R8 or any of sections 1-5 lacked a requirement, `every_requirement_area_has_a_requirement` fails naming the heading.

demonstrations.method: Typed deserialization with deny_unknown_fields plus enum checks; verifier also reads docs/spec.toml for plain statements and merged duplicates.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes; the file's requirements each show id, statement, kind, status and one or more sources.
demonstrations.fails_without: A requirement missing a field, with a kind or status outside the enums, would fail `the_spec_matches_the_brief` through serde errors and enum checks.

demonstrations.method: Read docs/spec.toml for [[open_question]] entries with two verbatim quotes, or the stated none-found reason; the test verifies quotes and that either one or the reason exists.
demonstrations.observes: Test passes; the file shows the open question(s) unresolved, or the explicit none statement.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the open-question field were not checked, `an_open_question_quote_not_in_the_brief_is_flagged` fails.

demonstrations.method: Run policy tests, which scan tracked files; the verifier also reads docs/spec.toml for such statements.
demonstrations.fails_without: If spec.toml named who runs Athena or where, `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where` fails.

demonstrations.method: Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0; this includes M24, so the new enforcement row's test names exist, and the ontology test accepts the new term.
demonstrations.fails_without: A lint, format or test failure would show as a non-zero exit.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff for CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] / Added and docs/decisions.md D111 (case, decision, alternatives Markdown with ids, JSON, YAML, tradeoff, reversal cost, provenance) including the note that sections 7-10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda follow in a second job.
demonstrations.observes: Both entries are present with those contents.

open_questions: Whether Olympus sections 1-6 contain a genuine conflict or open choice for the open_question field; the planner found none obvious (Section 5 'Neither loop owns the other' is a statement, not a conflict), so the producer must re-read and record none unless it finds one.
Whether xtask/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock need any change: toml and serde are already dev-dependencies of xtask, so likely none; the producer should confirm with cargo build --locked.
